questions.explanation: Percent means out of 100, so 35% is 35 out of every hundred.
questions.misconception: Percent always compares to exactly 100, not 10 or 1000 — that fixed scale is what makes it useful.

questions.prompt: How do you write 25% as a fraction?
questions.explanation: Percent means out of 100, so 25% = 25/100, which simplifies to 1/4.
questions.misconception: The 'out of 100' goes in the denominator; reversing to 100/25 or using 10 confuses the scale.

questions.prompt: How do you write 40% as a decimal?
questions.misconception: 0.04 would be 4% and 4.0 would be 400% — dividing by 100 moves the decimal two places to 0.40.
25% of 80 is not 25 — you must multiply the percent (as a decimal) by the number: 0.25 × 80 = 20.

questions.explanation: 100% means all 100 of every 100, so it is the whole amount.
questions.misconception: Only 100% (100 out of 100) is the entire whole; any smaller percent leaves part out.
